# Universal cell embedding (UCE)

## Takeaway

UCE learns a unified latent space for cells across tissues and species and can embed new data without dataset-specific fine-tuning. It is a useful recent zero-shot representation branch for annotation and cross-species exploration.

## Input and output

- Input: single-cell expression in AnnData-compatible form and a pinned UCE checkpoint.
- Output: zero-shot cell embeddings and downstream label-transfer or classifier inputs.
- Record: gene identifiers, protein-token vocabulary coverage, species, tissue, checkpoint and hardware.

## Official material

- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10689-z
- PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42420460/
- Code: https://github.com/snap-stanford/UCE
- Turnkey entry: python/07_uce_manifest.py in the methods catalog.

## Limitation

Zero-shot embeddings are still model outputs. Preserve the original expression analysis and compare marker-based or classical embedding baselines before using UCE to support a biological claim.
